Counties in Idaho are required by the legislature to perform certain services and programs for the public. From solid waste management, think Landfills, to operating a jail, providing driver’s license services, public safety, assessing the value of your property, and conducting elections, to name just a few. Almost every service provided by county government is required. As we approach FY26 budget presentations, we want you to know what services and programs we must provide. Knowing even a fraction of the services that we are required to provide you and your family gives you a better understanding of the decisions we make involving tax dollars. Please take a moment to look at some of the requirements put in place by the Idaho Legislature related to county government. 6 When a significant event is happening in your community where do you go to get trusted, consistent, and reliable information for yourself and your family? Ada County Public Information Officers, Community Outreach professionals as well as Training, and Education Staff serve a critically important role in facilitating communication between Ada County departments, elected offices, and the public— ensuring government transparency and keeping the public informed. PUBLIC INFORMATION AND GOVERNMENT TRANSPARENCY Ada County acknowledges the critically important work done to keep our communities informed From social media platforms to news releases, news conferences, newsletters and local government websites, those in the communications space work to ensure that you and your family know about important programs, initiatives and events happening in Ada County. Ada County Commissioners signed a proclamation in early May designating the month as PIO, Community Outreach, Training and Education Staff Month. Thank you to the Board of Commissioners for recognizing those who work each day to make sure our communities are well-informed and have access to reliable information every day. 54% of U.S. adults get their news from social media Source: Pew Research Center Some buildings feel good to be in. The folks in the photo below work every day to ensure the safety of every building in Ada County. Our building inspectors performed almost 8,000 inspections in 2024, with our most senior inspector averaging 227 inspections a month, or 10-12 per day. This work is in addition to team meetings, completing requirements for maintaining certifications, and driving time between sites. Even more remarkable - we only have three inspectors who cover the entire county. Another arm of the crucial Building Safety team is our permitting team. In March alone, the permitting team processed 307 applications, including 21 over-the- counter permits, a process for certain permit types where folks can walk into our office and walk out 30- 45 minutes later, permit in hand. MAY IS BUILDING SAFETY MONTH Our team is dedicated to efficiency, transparency, and safety, above all else. And finally, we can’t forget our engineers, who make sure buildings are safe from hazards like flooding and steep slopes. They also complete inspections and site visits, and often assist other departments and agencies across the valley. We are thrilled to celebrate them this month and share the important work they do to keep Ada County residents safe!

# Page 7^page=7
7 ADA COUNTY DEPARTMENT HEADS PRAISE RETIRING CITY OF BOISE COUNTERPARTS One of the best things about working collaboratively with our colleagues in city government is the relationships that develop over years of service. Those strong relationships benefit everyone who lives, works, and visits Ada County. City of Boise Parks & Recreation Director Doug Holloway retires at the end of October. “We would like to express our congratulations to Boise Parks and Recreation Director Doug Holloway on his retirement. Over the years, Doug has played a pivotal role in fostering Ada County’s collaborative partnership with Boise Parks and Recreation. His dedication to cultivating relationships, promoting outdoor recreation, and ensuring accessible outdoor experiences has greatly enriched our community. It has truly been a privilege to work alongside him, and we wish him all the best in this new chapter of his life.” Scott Koberg, Director, Ada County Parks & Waterways Boise Fire Chief Mark Niemeyer retires at the end of November. “Mark Niemeyer started his career in Idaho with Ada County Paramedics. After moving to the Meridian Fire Department, he was instrumental in the formation of the Ada County-City Emergency Medical Services System. Mark has a heart for collaboration and bringing folks together. He has done an outstanding job at Boise Fire, and we wish him the best in retirement.” Shawn Rayne, Ada County Paramedics Chief Wishing Doug Holloway and Mark Niemeyer all the best in retirement. From everyone in Ada County thank you for your years of work and contributions in making our communities healthy, and safe and vibrant places. City of Boise Parks and Recreation Director Doug Holloway City of Boise Fire Chief Mark Niemeyer

# Page 8^page=8
8 Congratulations to Garden City Mayor John Evans on his early retirement. We say early because it seems way too early for this Treasure Valley leader to move on from the position he’s held for twenty years. When John was first elected Mayor of Garden City, the population was around 10 thousand. Now, Garden City has more than 13 thousand residents. Since Garden City is landlocked within the center of Boise, the growth had to be upward, right? If you’ve lived in Idaho for the last twenty years you have watched as Garden City has morphed into a modern and exciting city. Garden City had its challenges decades ago. Now, when you drive down Chinden Blvd., you see stylish new restaurants, brew pubs, shops, galleries, and a variety of places that make a city vibrant and enjoyable. John has been a consistent partner on many projects with Ada County over the years. His city has graciously welcomed fairgoers each year in August for the annual Western Idaho Fair. While the Fair happens on Ada County property it sits within the center of Garden City. John has been a great partner on projects like the Boise River Greenbelt, which also winds its way through Garden City, and of course the eagerly awaited Park at Expo Idaho and Professional soccer. County commissions must work with multiple cities that have diverse constituents with different tastes and priorities. Not everyone sees a project the same way. What sounds good for GARDEN CITY MAYOR JOHN EVANS TO RETIRE one geographical entity may not work for people who live nearby. John has been a masterful collaborator as the Treasure Valley navigated the choppy waters of unprecedented growth. John, as you move on to new endeavors, please always know what a significant and lasting impact you had on one of Idaho’s most beloved and eclectic cities. You have made a difference in the Treasure Valley. We look forward to seeing you at an upcoming professional soccer game or meandering through The Park at Expo Idaho in late 2026. Happy Trails.

# Page 9^page=9
9 Tuesday May 20, 2025 was the opening night game for the Boise Hawks at Memorial Stadium. Ada County Commissioners – Chairman Rod Beck, Ryan Davidson, and Tom Dayley were honored to throw out the first pitches! While the final score wasn’t what the home team wanted – The Idaho Falls Chukars beat the Hawks 9-3 … the weather was perfect, and the Hawks can swoop in for victories as the season continues. Thank you, Boise Hawks. Wishing the team a successful 2025 Season! CONSTRUCTION CONTINUES ON THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO Monthly videos highlight the amazing transformation The 50-acre park is set to open in late 2026. The park at the corner of Glenwood and Chinden will include nature trails, world class skate park areas, pavilions, a food truck area and much more. Follow along as this once-in-a-generation park becomes reality. Be sure and watch our monthly progress videos with incredible drone footage on Ada County’s YouTube. MONTHLY PARK PROGRESS VIDEOS

10 June is one of the busiest months for counties in Idaho. That’s when FY26 budgets are presented to the Board of Commissioners. Next month, we’ll share highlights from the presentations we told you about earlier in this newsletter. Ada County’s fiscal year begins October 1, 2025. A much-anticipated announcement happens June 27th as Boise Pro Soccer unveils the Team Name, Team Crest, and Team Colors for Idaho’s first professional soccer team! What do you think the name will be? Professional soccer games begin in March of next year, and we couldn’t be more excited! Also, as the 4th of July Holiday approaches, we’ll explain in detail why Unincorporated Ada County has a fireworks ban in place. Two words: Your Safety. Thank you for reading the Ada County Newsletter. Remember to sign up to receive the newsletter automatically every month.
